To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a mathematical model for the interaction of two mutually attractive/repulsive species, which is able to describe the formation of phase separated regions, and that we have proved rigorously the occurrence of such a phenomenon.
we prove that the support of the solution of a continuum model for a two species system is simply connected and has zero Lebesgues measure.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a mathematical model for two species interacting via a short range repulsion and two long range attractions.
the mathematical analysis of a model describing the dynamics of the population density of two interacting species.
the mathematical analysis of the stationary solutions to a model of two mutually attracting/repelling species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two species are separated from each other, and each species occupies its own region.
the model predicts a phase separation in the form of a single connected domain for the total density of the two species.
in the present case, the two species do not mix, but rather form two separate regions, each of the two regions being occupied by one of the species only.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the two species do not coexist, and that the system is in a steady state.
, in the case that the two species are repelling, we prove the phase separation of the two species, i.e., the two species are segregated.

we prove the existence of a stationary solution for a system of two species with different self- and cross attraction, and we show that this solution exhibits a phase separation into two regions, each of them containing one species only.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the two species are separated by an interface, which is a smooth curve.
the two species are not able to co-exist in the long run in a region where both species are present.
, even if the species are not competing for the same resource, they may still be segregated.
